didYouKnow: Tobacco kills up to half of its long-term users — over 8.7 million people every year.
Over 1.3 million non-smokers die annually from exposure to secondhand smoke.
Tobacco use costs the global economy an estimated $1.8 Trillion USD in healthcare costs and lost productivity every year.
Global tobacco smoking prevalence has dropped from 32.7% in 2000 to 20.9% today due to WHO MPOWER policies.

faq.q: How many people die from tobacco use each year?
faq.a: Tobacco kills more than 8.7 million people per year worldwide, including 7.4 million direct smokers and 1.3 million non-smokers exposed to secondhand smoke.

faq.q: How many smokers are there in the world?
faq.a: There are approximately 1.3 billion tobacco users globally, with roughly 1.05 billion males and 250 million females.
